rule: every behaviour below is referenced by >= 1 scenario (active or pending); every NIST reference in a scenario is listed here

behaviours.title: Detect periodic command-and-control check-ins (network-based IDPS, anomaly detection)
Correlate the same indicator across several hosts
Detect anomalous DNS use (generated names, tunnelling, rewritten answers)
Detect unusual outbound data transfer
Detect activity spread over long periods below per-interval thresholds (evasion by timing)
Detect internal reconnaissance and lateral movement
Detect scanning and brute-force fan-out
Signature-based detection, with its false-positive limits
Policy-based detection (e.g. disallowed destinations)
Detect exposed services and inbound-initiated sessions
Detect link-layer and name-service attacks (ARP, DHCP, RA, LLMNR/NBNS)
Detect denial-of-service participation
Detect destructive activity on file shares
Detect resource hijacking (mining, proxyware)
Resist evasion: encryption, tunnelling, trusted services, rotation, mimicry
Tuning: benign activity must not alert (false-positive control)
Benign events that affect many hosts at once must not page
Sensor overload and packet loss are recorded, not treated as clean
The IDPS monitors and protects itself
Detection and analysis: precursors and indicators from the first observation
Analysis: an incident rests on related evidence, not unrelated coincidences
Containment: holds, honours approvals, does not loop
Recovery: return after offline / restart resumes the incident correctly
Post-incident activity: outcomes feed learning, wrong learning is revoked
Log time integrity: clock jumps are detected and handled
Late, out-of-order or duplicated log records are ordered by event time
Missing log spans are recorded as gaps, never as 'nothing happened'
